body:
Looking through the code, I see this comment:
https://github.com/starship/starship/blob/a10e24b2052047d431b6a44b0a202f605c39bc96/src/modules/status.rs#L20

Seems like a rather odd choice.  Why to restrict the user from displaying success status if he wishes to?
Since it can easily be disabled by default by using: `success_symbol = ""`.

Also why is `success_symbol` needed if "display the status only if it is not 0"?

Thank you for opening this issue.  Good to know I am not alone 😄 

I was trying to do the same thing when I first started using `starship` but I was a noob and thought I am probably doing something wrong so just gave up.

Definitely looks like an oversight.
I'd suggest making the change you proposed, setting the default `success_symbol` to be an empty string and outputting `success_symbol` on non-zero status codes. 👍
I actually already made [changes to my fork](https://github.com/IzhakJakov/starship) and they work (for me) as intended.

Thank you :)
I would love to try this but I am not sure how to build this project 😅 
Did not see any build instructions on the main page.

Hmm...
I don't know if you need to do anything special. All I did was `cargo build --release`.
I mean make sure you have `cargo` installed then clone the repo then `cd` to it and run `cargo build --release`.
Will do.  Thank you! 🙇‍♂️

> I mean make sure you have `cargo` installed then clone the repo then `cd` to it and run `cargo build --release`.

I tried your changes but it did not work for me 😞
May I know which shell you are using?
I am using `fish` but also tried on `bash` and did not work for me 😅

Just tried and both `bash` and `fish` are working for me.
Would you mind sharing your `starship.toml` ?
BTW, what version of the shell are you using?

I am using `fish, version 3.4.0`.

Here are my setting:
```toml
format = """
Execution $status $cmd_duration
$line_break\
$directory$character\
"""

[character]
vicmd_symbol = '\([CMD](bold yellow)\)❯'
success_symbol = '\([INS](bold green)\)❯'
error_symbol = '\([INS](bold green)\)❯'

[status]
format = '$symbol$success_symbol'
disabled = false
symbol = '[crashed](bold red)'
success_symbol = '[finished](bold green)'

[cmd_duration]
min_time = 0
format = 'after [$duration]($style).'

[directory]
format = '\[$path\][$read_only]($read_only_style)'
read_only = '🔒 '
```

OK we are using the same `fish` version.
I tried your config and it works for me on `bash` and `fish`:
```
[/]🔒 (INS) ❯ echo 'Hello World!'
Hello World!

Execution finished after 0ms.

[/]🔒 (CMD) ❯ echp 'Hello World!'
fish: Unknown command: echp

Execution crashed after 0ms.
```
Are you sourcing the new `starship` build from `target/release`?

Replace `starship init fish | source` in `~/.config/fish/config.fish` with `<local_path_to_starship_repo>/target/release/starship init fish | source`.
Start a new shell and LMK if still does not work.

Yes this work :)
Can you fix it in the next version of `starship` so I can continue using `starship init fish | source`?

Well I will create a PR after I follow @matchai's [request](https://github.com/starship/starship/issues/3746#issuecomment-1067054043) and change the default value of `success_symbol` then modify the documentation to reflect the changes.
Afterwards it needs to get approved and merged but I can't guarantee which version of `starship` will have the changes since it's not up to me.

Oh OK. Hopefully soon 🤞 
Thank you for fixing it 🙇‍♂️   You are awesome!! 😄
After this change is there any way to have no symbol if the overall pipeline succeeded, but a checkmark within the pipestatus for successful sub-processes of a failing pipeline?
Can you please provide "expected" vs "actual"?

Also can you please provide the following:
1. Shell you are using
2. Starship config you are using
3. Command you call before the "expected"/"actual" prompt

(Simplified to remove extra modules and unicode characters) config:
```toml
format = """
($status )$character
"""

[character]
success_symbol = ">"
error_symbol = "[>](red)"
vicmd_symbol = "[>](yellow)"

[status]
disabled = false
symbol = "X"
success_symbol = "Y"
format = "[$symbol]($style)"
pipestatus_separator = " | "
pipestatus_format = "\\[ $pipestatus \\] = [$symbol]($style)"
map_symbol = true
pipestatus = true
```

Previously this looked like this:

```console
> starship --version
starship 1.0.0
branch:master
commit_hash:6061cae5
build_time:2021-12-15 19:34:45 +00:00
build_env:rustc 1.57.0 (Arch Linux rust 1:1.57.0-1),

> true | true

> true | false

[ Y | X ] = X >
```

(yes, that's a very old version, I had this version lying around to test with and noticed the change from a much more recent one).

After the update:

```console
Y > starship --version
starship 1.5.4
tag:v1.5.4
commit_hash:d420a63e
build_time:2022-03-24 19:52:40 +00:00
build_env:rustc 1.59.0 (Arch Linux rust 1:1.59.0-1),

Y > true | true

[ Y | Y ] = Y > true | false

[ Y | X ] = X >
```

If I set `success_symbol = ""` then it stops showing the status when the command was successful, but it also shows just a blank segment in the `pipestatus` for that command when the pipeline fails.

EDIT: Oh, and `zsh` for the shell.

So I am guessing it would be something like that:
```
> true | true

> true | false

[ | X ] = X >
```
I wonder if pipestatus should have a separate success symbol... 🤔
Or maybe some variable like `success=never`, `success=always`, `success=onlypipe`.

What is your opinion about `success_pipe=Y`, `error_pipe=X`?
If not set, defaults to `success_symbol`, `error_symbol`...

> What is your opinion about `success_pipe=Y`, `error_pipe=X`?

That sounds pretty good to me.
OK great now I need to find the time to look into this.
I think we need another issue to track this.  I think you could describe it better than me but if you want help, then I'll do it.  LMK
